# 油價升破$95，短端美債續受壓，信用供給面臨考驗

## 能源成本提高，融資需求卻仍持續增加

美國與伊朗局勢再升級，布蘭特原油升至$95.37，美債繼續下跌。2年期殖利率上升5個基點至4.31%，10年期上升4個基點至4.67%，30年期上升2個基點至5.15%。投資人衡量能源成本若持續偏高，是否迫使聯準會更強力回應，較短天期因而繼續承受較大調整。

與前一天不同，10年期名目殖利率增幅由實質殖利率與通膨補償各占一半：兩者均升2個基點，分別達2.39%、2.28%。外交停滯、區域基礎設施受威脅，使石油供應干擾持續影響前景，即使全部效果尚未反映在美國通膨數據。能源提高營運費用之際，實質殖利率也增加了房市與投資成本。

資金仍可取得，但借款人之間的差異更明顯。科威特在攻擊與出口受阻下，仍以強勁需求完成$60億美元債。Galaxy Digital準備以CoreWeave相關大型專案進入高收益債市場，北歐資料中心業者卻難以完成發行。Cable One面對兩位數借款成本及資產隔離要求，Aston Martin則在債權人提出法律挑戰後取得新擔保融資。資本沒有消失，但能否取得，愈來愈取決於提供什麼資產、現金流與債權保障。

## 短端領跌，長端殖利率仍居高檔

5年期殖利率上升4個基點至4.41%。升幅向長端遞減，使2s10s收窄1個基點至36個基點，2s30s收窄3個基點至84個基點。一週變化更明顯，2年期、5年期、10年期、30年期分別上升18、15、12、7個基點；一個月升幅則為12、18、21、25個基點，顯示最近短端加速調整，但較長期間累積的壓力仍以長端較大。

各觀察天期實質殖利率均上升2個基點。5年期達2.11%、7年期2.24%、20年期2.73%、30年期2.93%，10年期為2.39%。通膨補償的反應比週二更大，實質利率上升也相當廣泛。投資人同時要求補償未來物價可能更高，以及政策可能因此維持緊縮更久的風險。

交易時段內，能源消息持續惡化。美國與伊朗仍距恢復談判甚遠，攻擊升級，威脅延伸至橋梁、電廠與區域能源設施。布蘭特升破$95時，美債同步走弱。市場擔心的是燃料與運輸流動可能更長時間受阻，而不只是一天的商品價格變化。

較長天期短券也重新定價。17週券殖利率升5個基點至3.94%，52週券升3個基點至4.10%，4至8週券則仍接近3.71%至3.73%。這使焦點留在政策期間，而非立即缺乏現金；相較先前降息預期，市場更重視2026年稍後升息的可能。

長債當天相對抗跌，但起點已相當高。30年期已連續12個交易日收在5%以上，2026年共有27天曾交易於這個門檻之上。美國公債市場由2007年約$4.5兆擴大至約$31兆，聯邦年度利息支出也超過$1兆。

政府還需與超過$5,000億AI相關融資，爭取部分相同的退休金、保險及其他長天期資金。殖利率超過5%，已不再像過去一些時期那樣迅速吸引買盤。週三長端較穩，並沒有消除這項競爭，只是顯示最新賣壓更接近聯準會政策路徑。

## AI專案仍能融資，條件卻不能一概而論

Galaxy Digital計畫為Helios資料中心園區首次發行$35億高收益債，5年期券討論殖利率約9%。CoreWeave的15年容量租約，預估每年帶來超過$10億收入。擬發債另規劃從完工後10個月起，每年償還原始本金4%，讓投資人在園區營運後逐步降低曝險。

這筆交易將接在2026年美國資料中心開發商已籌得約$280億高收益債之後。合約收入有助專案融資，但建設、租戶集中度，以及債權相對專案層級負債的位置仍然重要。租戶知名，不代表不同結構的風險就相同。

銀行融資也在增加。Blackstone旗下AirTrunk正籌組承銷銀行，為SYD3園區安排A$43億、折合$30億的5年建設貸款，同時完成另一筆約$23億馬來西亞貸款。今年AI基礎設施債券與貸款已達至少$3,345億，2025全年則為$1,855億。即使整個產業所需資金遠超過前一年，個別專案仍能吸引銀行。

歐洲較小的北歐市場，限制出現得更快。Prime Data Centers把挪威法交易由$6億縮至$5億後仍撤案，Pure Data Centres也放棄€10億債券，改用銀行融資；先前H.I.G.支持的交易則曾籌得紀錄€8億。差別不在市場是否曾經打開，而在成功承接最初交易後，還能容納多少接續而來的複雜發行。

投資人必須比較合約EBITDA、貸款成數，以及位於營運資產負債之上的持股公司債權。持股公司債權人可能在結構上次於專案貸款人，卻仍承擔開發風險。保障條件各異，不能只以同一個AI產業故事取代對還款結構的檢視。

Cable One的融資價格限制更直接。約$10億第一順位方案，討論殖利率約12%，用於履行收購Mega Broadband剩餘55%股權的義務並處理到期債。貸款人要求資產隔離，將兩項業務分開，避免Cable One補貼Mega Broadband債務。

方案需支付GTCR約$4.75億至$4.95億，其餘可用於Cable One的2028、2029年債務。穆迪已降評至B2，約$30億長期負債大部分殖利率達兩位數。先前交換案只有34%貸款人參與，低於約50%的早期門檻。高殖利率、優先擔保及移轉限制，是新融資的核心條件。

Aston Martin則已取得現金。HPS以£4.5億優先擔保定期貸款及£1億延遲動用額度，提供合計£5.5億，另保留£1億次順位債空間。所得將償還£1.7億循環額度及股東借款。這筆安排在既有債權人挑戰之後強化了短期流動性，但方式是在$18.5億既有債券持有人之外新增擔保借款，而不是這些債券重新獲得信任。

市政債投資人也在定價具體營運限制。Corpus Christi近期10年期債券利差60個基點，高於類似El Paso券的40個基點，儘管兩個地方政府均為AA。這個德州南部系統服務約50萬人，可能在2027年耗盡水源；其公用事業債另於5月被標普降兩級至A，6月被惠譽降三級至A-。水資源風險已影響融資成本，而非只是遙遠的環境情境。

Varta則顯示先前紓困的限制。談判無法取得新資金後，債權人著手分拆消費電池部門；他們先前已接受大幅減記，並在2025年重整後提供€6,000萬。營運繼續惡化，使保存價值的方法轉向掌握資產，而非再單純展延到期。

LQD下跌0.17%至106.67，HYG與JNK各跌0.16%，分別為79.52、95.75。基金小跌之際，融資仍存在但差異擴大。固定收益收盤後，銀行開始分銷$350億Broadcom-Anthropic融資的部分部位，包括$240億一部分，指示價格約100至100.5。這是大型私人融資進一步流向銀行與機構持有人的後續消息，增加下一輪供給，而非解釋已完成的當日價格。

## 英國通膨降溫未帶動英債，日本政策預期轉鷹

英國6月通膨降至2.6%，為逾一年最低，也是連續第三次低於預期。英債卻仍下跌，2年期與5年期殖利率各升5個基點至4.44%、4.63%，指標殖利率維持5%以上。6月數據反映的燃料降價，已被最新油價上漲追過。

能源變貴可能傳到服務、薪資及每季調整的家庭能源價格上限，使英國央行回到2%通膨更困難。先前借款規則彈性引發爭論後，首相伯納姆的支出目標又增加財政層面的疑慮。政府若要減輕家庭負擔，可能需要在能源重新推高物價時增加借款。

日本方面，報導指出央行官員願意考慮比經濟學家原估約每半年更快升息，帶動市場重新定價。交換市場估計10月以前升息機率約84%，高於先前約72%。日圓已貶破163兌$1，接近約40年低點。

官員認為基礎通膨接近2%，伊朗衝突後企業轉嫁成本也加快。日圓轉弱提高進口能源及原料價格，強化了國內通膨所支持的升息理由。政策並非追求某個匯率目標，但匯率會改變央行想控制的價格。

長債需求提供了另一股力量。40年期日本公債標售吸引2025年3月以來最強需求，殖利率約3.91%，低於5月紀錄4.355%；標售後日債變化不大。相較先前保險公司買進的資料，這次是當前標售的直接測試：短端預期更快正常化，並未阻止投資人認為超長債殖利率已有價值。

日本債務超過GDP的200%，使融資成本與政策辯論難以分開。鼓勵國內機構持有長債，可能穩住市場，也可能使資金從美債回流。對全球投資人而言，這是較高的日本預期短率，加上長端仍有本地買方，而非所有日本公債都同步走弱。

## 海灣國家資產實力與亞洲本地買盤承受衝擊

科威特在持續攻擊、出口受阻下，仍以3年期、5年期、10年期美元債籌得$60億。最終訂單約$148億，使三個年期利差均較初步指引收緊25個基點。即使衝突損壞電力及供水設施、迫使大部分石油出口停止，評等、主權財富及較高美債基準殖利率仍支持需求。

交易為嚴重營運與財政衝擊提供了流動性。大部分出口停頓，即使富裕主權也會面對收入大幅中斷。強勁訂單顯示資產負債表實力可以保住融資管道，不代表國家不受石油收入損失影響。

泰國本地債市有不同支撐：通膨受控、預定發行減少。7月15日10年期標售投標倍數2.18倍，為8月以來最強；其後2029年到期券達2.13倍，為1月以來最佳。會計年度發行預估THB1.26兆，較原先THB1.3兆計畫少約3%。

6月通膨為2.42%，低於預估2.7%。經濟學家預測中位數認為，10年期殖利率到2027年6月底會降至1.73%，比當時低約25個基點。這個展望立基於成長偏弱、價格壓力受控及供給有利，而不是假設最新全球能源風險已消失。

南非則面對相反的通膨意外。6月CPI由4.5%升至5.0%，高於中位數預估4.7%。10年期政府債殖利率盤中上升約10個基點至8.79%，之後回吐部分升幅。運輸、住宅與公用事業、保險及金融服務帶動超預期，能源與肥料成本也增加回到3%目標的風險。

市場偏向預期南非央行升息25個基點至7.25%，但廣泛第二輪效應仍有限，也保留維持利率、搭配鷹派指引的空間。兩年後通膨預期由3.6%升至3.9%，無論如何決定，維持公信力都重要。

印尼在5月、6月累計升息100個基點後，維持BI-Rate於5.75%，印尼盾與10年期殖利率穩定。6月整體通膨達3.34%，接近1.5%至3.5%目標區間上緣，核心通膨預期低於3%。暫停升息有利活動，但仍需匯率及進口價格保持可控。

迦納同樣維持14%，6月通膨由3.7%升至5.3%。公用事業費率、中東升級與原油，都是相對6%至10%中期目標區間的上行風險。斯里蘭卡5月已升息100個基點，這次維持隔夜利率8.75%，即使通膨連續第三個月超過5%目標。土耳其預期連續第四次維持一週附買回利率37%，並繼續透過40%隔夜利率供資，等待7月通膨及能源局勢更明確。

本地與海外融資也有差異。銅收入及政策延續預期支持尚比亞克瓦查債，今年美元報酬達36%，廣泛新興市場本幣債指數只有1.35%。短端殖利率14.25%、較長天期17.5%，選舉結果預期將影響下一次標售。坦尚尼亞則以倫敦路演測試2013年以來首次硬通貨發債需求，整體計畫借入約$17億外國資金。

阿根廷主權信心改善，尚未修復家庭信用。在極高利率下快速擴張貸款後，銀行逾放升至20年高點，促使授信更有選擇性，也延後借款帶動復甦的期待。EMB下跌0.30%至95.09，因此涵蓋海灣強勁發行、泰國有利供給，以及其他市場更緊的條件，並不需要新的美元大漲才會發生。

## 油價與黃金走高，波動率卻未全面升高

布蘭特上漲4.79%至$95.37，WTI上漲3.34%至$87.75。漲幅使能源直接反映在當天較高的損益兩平通膨率與短端美債殖利率。有緩衝的出口國，以及面對補貼、經常帳成本的進口國，承受方式不同。

股市漲跌互見。S&P 500下跌0.14%，Nasdaq 100下跌0.54%，半導體卻上漲0.44%，VIX下降2.40%至16.64。投資人等待AI高額支出的回報證據，晶片買盤仍帶動大盤脫離低點。半導體比一個月前仍低13.47%，因此一天收漲並未解決融資與估值爭論。

美元指數下降0.06%至101.122，一週仍高0.62%。即使沒有另一波當日匯率衝擊，實質殖利率與油價提高也足以壓抑新興債。黃金反而在實質殖利率上升下漲1.50%至$4,132.10，地緣政治避險蓋過平常的不利因素。能源與政策疑慮清楚可見，卻未伴隨股市波動率大升或融資信心全面流失。

## 數據與新發行將測試重新定價的界線

7月24日新屋銷售、7月27日耐久財訂單初值，以及7月28日經濟指標預估報告，接著就是7月28至29日FOMC。數據將協助判斷，需求是否仍強到讓能源衝擊促使央行更有力回應，或是高借款成本已提供足夠抑制。

Galaxy Digital預計7月23日定價，是北歐受挫後對美國高收益債承接能力的直接測試。規模、殖利率及次級表現，將顯示CoreWeave租約與擬定攤還安排，是否足以支持約9%殖利率、$35億計畫。完成交易可以建立這個結構的可行條件，不代表整個產業的融資需求都能無限吸收。

7月23日南非央行及7月31日日本銀行會議，將顯示進口能源如何影響不同政策架構。南非部分取決於第二輪效應與預期，日本則重視基礎通膨、匯率傳導及正常化速度。指引影響當地短端與貨幣，日本長債承接則仍攸關可投入海外債券的資金。

long_thesis.english_markdown:
# Oil above $95 keeps pressure on short Treasuries and tests credit supply

## Higher energy costs meet a crowded market for capital

Treasuries fell again as renewed US-Iran escalation sent Brent to $95.37. The 2-year yield rose 5 basis points to 4.31%, while the 10-year added 4 to 4.67% and the 30-year 2 to 5.15%. Shorter maturities continued to absorb more of the adjustment as investors weighed the possibility that persistent energy costs would require a firmer Fed response.

Unlike the preceding session, the 10-year move was evenly split between real yields and inflation compensation: both rose 2 basis points, to 2.39% and 2.28%. Stalled diplomacy and threats to regional infrastructure kept oil disruption in the forward outlook, even though its full effect had not yet appeared in US inflation releases. A higher real yield added to the cost of housing and investment just as energy raised operating expenses.

Funding remained available, but the contrast between borrowers was becoming sharper. Kuwait placed $6 billion of dollar bonds with substantial demand despite attacks and disrupted exports. Galaxy Digital approached the junk market with a large CoreWeave-linked project, while Nordic data-center issuers had struggled to complete deals. Cable One faced double-digit borrowing costs and creditor demands to separate assets; Aston Martin obtained new secured liquidity after its bondholders' legal challenge. Capital had not disappeared, but access increasingly turned on the assets, cash flows and creditor rights offered in return.

## The front end leads while long yields stay elevated

The 5-year yield rose 4 basis points to 4.41%. With gains diminishing toward the long end, 2s10s narrowed 1 basis point to 36 and 2s30s narrowed 3 to 84. The weekly pattern was more pronounced: yields were up 18, 15, 12 and 7 basis points at two, five, ten and 30 years. That front-led repricing contrasted with monthly increases of 12, 18, 21 and 25 basis points, which still reflected a larger accumulated burden at longer maturities.

Real yields rose 2 basis points at every quoted maturity. Five years ended at 2.11%, seven at 2.24%, 20 at 2.73% and 30 at 2.93%, alongside the 10-year's 2.39%. Inflation compensation responded more strongly than on Tuesday, but the real-rate increase was also broad. Investors were paying for both the possibility of higher future inflation and the prospect of policy remaining restrictive in response.

The energy news was active during trading. The US and Iran remained far from returning to negotiations, attacks escalated and threats extended to bridges, power plants and regional energy infrastructure. Brent moved above $95 as Treasuries weakened. The resulting concern was about a longer interruption to fuel and freight flows, not simply a one-day commodity price change.

Further-out bills also repriced. The 17-week yield rose 5 basis points to 3.94% and the 52-week 3 to 4.10%, while 4- to 8-week yields remained close to 3.71%–3.73%. That difference kept the focus on the policy horizon rather than an immediate cash shortage. The market was assigning greater weight to possible hikes later in 2026 after earlier expectations of cuts.

Long bonds outperformed on the day, but from an unusually high starting point. The 30-year had closed above 5% for 12 consecutive sessions and traded beyond that level on 27 days during 2026. Treasury debt outstanding had expanded to about $31 trillion from $4.5 trillion in 2007, while annual federal interest expense exceeded $1 trillion.

Government supply was competing with more than $500 billion of AI-linked financing for overlapping pension, insurance and other long-duration portfolios. A yield above 5% was no longer drawing the rapid buying response seen in some earlier episodes. Wednesday's relative long-end resilience did not remove that competition; it showed that the latest selling pressure was closer to the expected Fed path.

## AI projects find funding, but not on interchangeable terms

Galaxy Digital planned a debut $3.5 billion high-yield issue for its Helios data-center campus, with five-year notes discussed around a 9% yield. CoreWeave's 15-year capacity lease was expected to produce more than $1 billion of annual revenue. The proposed notes would repay 4% of original principal annually beginning ten months after construction completion, giving investors a scheduled reduction in exposure once the campus was operating.

The transaction would follow about $28 billion raised by data-center developers in the US junk market during 2026. Contracted revenue helped make projects financeable, but construction, tenant concentration and where a creditor sat relative to project-level debt remained important. A familiar tenant did not make different structures equivalent.

Bank financing was expanding as well. Blackstone-owned AirTrunk was assembling underwriters for an A$4.3 billion, or $3 billion, five-year construction loan for its SYD3 campus, while completing another roughly $2.3 billion loan for Malaysia. AI infrastructure bonds and loans had already reached at least $334.5 billion for the year, compared with $185.5 billion in all of 2025. Individual projects could still attract lenders even as the sector's aggregate financing requirement far exceeded the previous year's total.

Europe's smaller Nordic market had shown a more immediate limit. Prime Data Centers shelved its Norwegian-law deal after reducing the proposed size from $600 million to $500 million, and Pure Data Centres abandoned a €1 billion bond in favor of bank funding. An earlier H.I.G.-backed issue had raised a record €800 million. The contrast was not between a market that existed and one that never opened, but between a successful initial placement and the capacity to absorb repeated complex offerings.

Investors had to compare contracted EBITDA, loan-to-value measures and claims issued above operating-asset debt. Holding-company creditors could be structurally subordinated to project lenders while retaining exposure to development risk. Differences in those protections made a single AI-sector narrative a poor substitute for examining individual repayment structures.

Cable One's proposed financing faced a more acute price constraint. A roughly $1 billion first-lien package, discussed around a 12% yield, would fund its required purchase of the remaining 55% of Mega Broadband and address maturities. Lenders sought ring-fencing to keep the businesses separate and prevent Cable One from subsidizing Mega Broadband's debt.

The package needed to cover a $475 million–$495 million payment to GTCR, with remaining proceeds available for Cable One's 2028 and 2029 debt. Moody's had cut the company to B2, and most of its roughly $3 billion of long-term obligations yielded in double digits. An earlier exchange drew only 34% lender participation against an approximately 50% early threshold. High yield, secured priority and limits on transfers were central to the new financing under discussion.

Aston Martin, by contrast, had now secured cash. HPS provided £550 million through a £450 million senior secured term loan and a £100 million delayed-draw facility, with capacity for another £100 million of junior debt. Proceeds would repay a £170 million revolver and shareholder loans. The package followed the existing bondholders' challenge and strengthened near-term liquidity, but did so through new secured borrowing outside the holders of $1.85 billion of existing notes rather than renewed confidence in those bonds.

Municipal investors were also pricing a concrete operating constraint. Corpus Christi's recent 10-year bonds carried a 60-basis-point spread, versus 40 for a comparable El Paso bond despite both municipalities' AA ratings. The south Texas system serves about 500,000 people and could run out of water in 2027. Its utility debt had separately been cut two notches to A by S&P in May and three to A- by Fitch in June. Water risk was already affecting financing costs, not merely appearing as a distant environmental scenario.

Varta showed the limits of a previous rescue. Creditors moved to separate the consumer-battery division after talks failed to secure fresh funding. They had already accepted a significant haircut and supplied €60 million after the 2025 restructuring. Continued deterioration left control over assets, rather than another simple extension of maturities, as the means of trying to preserve value.

LQD fell 0.17% to 106.67, while HYG and JNK each declined 0.16%, to 79.52 and 95.75. Those modest fund losses coexisted with available but increasingly differentiated financing. After the fixed-income close, banks began distributing pieces of a $35 billion Broadcom-Anthropic package, including a $24 billion tranche, at indicated prices around 100–100.5. That later development showed another large private financing moving toward bank and institutional holders, adding to the next round of supply rather than explaining the completed day's prices.

## Softer UK inflation fails to rally gilts; Japan's policy path shifts

UK June inflation slowed to 2.6%, the lowest in more than a year and the third consecutive downside surprise. Gilts nevertheless weakened: 2- and 5-year yields each rose 5 basis points to 4.44% and 4.63%, while benchmark yields stayed above 5%. Cheaper fuel in the June data was being overtaken by the new oil surge.

Higher energy costs could feed services, wages and the quarterly household price cap, complicating the BOE's return to 2%. Prime Minister Andy Burnham's spending ambitions added a fiscal dimension after the preceding debate over flexibility within borrowing rules. Measures intended to cushion households could require additional borrowing just as energy costs renewed price pressure.

In Japan, reporting that BOJ officials were open to raising rates faster than the roughly six-month cadence expected by economists moved market pricing. Swaps assigned about an 84% chance of an increase by October, up from roughly 72%. The yen had weakened beyond 163 per dollar, near its lowest levels in about four decades.

Officials saw underlying inflation approaching 2% and faster corporate pass-through following the Iran conflict. A weaker currency made imported energy and materials more expensive, reinforcing the domestic inflation case for action. The issue was not an exchange-rate target, though the currency affected the prices policymakers were trying to control.

Long-bond demand provided a counterweight. A 40-year JGB auction attracted the strongest demand since March 2025, with the yield around 3.91%, below May's record 4.355%. Japanese bonds were little changed after the sale. The result extended the prior evidence of insurer buying with a current auction test: faster expected normalization at the front end did not prevent investors from finding value in super-long yields.

Japan's debt, above 200% of GDP, kept funding costs entangled with the policy debate. Encouraging domestic institutions to hold long bonds could help anchor that market, but could also redirect savings from Treasuries. For global investors, the combination was a higher expected Japanese short-rate path and a functioning domestic buyer base at longer maturities, not uniform JGB weakness.

## Gulf balance-sheet strength and Asian demand withstand the shock

Kuwait raised $6 billion in 3-, 5- and 10-year dollar bonds despite repeated attacks and disrupted exports. Orders reached about $14.8 billion at final terms, allowing all three spreads to tighten 25 basis points from initial indications. Its rating, sovereign wealth and high reference Treasury yields supported demand even as the conflict damaged power and water infrastructure and forced most oil exports to stop.

The transaction provided liquidity against a severe operating and fiscal shock. With most exports halted, even a wealthy sovereign faced a substantial interruption to revenue. Strong orders showed that balance-sheet strength could preserve access; they did not mean the state was insulated from lost oil income.

Thailand's domestic bond market had a different support: contained inflation and lower planned issuance. The July 15 ten-year auction was covered 2.18 times, the strongest since August, and a subsequent 2029 sale 2.13 times, the best since January. Fiscal-year issuance was projected at THB1.26 trillion, about 3% below the original THB1.3 trillion plan.

June inflation was 2.42%, below the 2.7% estimate. The median economist forecast put the 10-year yield at 1.73% by end-June 2027, roughly 25 basis points below the prevailing level. That outlook rested on subdued growth, contained price pressure and favorable supply, rather than assuming the latest global energy risk had disappeared.

South Africa faced the opposite inflation surprise. June CPI accelerated to 5.0% from 4.5%, above the 4.7% median estimate. Ten-year government yields rose roughly 10 basis points to an intraday 8.79% before retracing part of the move. Transport, housing and utilities, insurance and financial services drove the surprise, while energy and fertilizer costs added risk to the return toward the 3% target.

Markets leaned toward a quarter-point SARB increase to 7.25%. Yet limited broad second-round effects left room for a hold with hawkish guidance. Two-year-ahead inflation expectations had risen to 3.9% from 3.6%, making credibility important whichever decision the bank chose.

Indonesia held its BI-Rate at 5.75% after 100 basis points of tightening in May and June. The rupiah and 10-year yield were steady. Headline inflation had reached 3.34% in June, near the top of the 1.5%–3.5% target range, while core inflation was expected below 3%. A hold supported activity but still depended on the currency and imported prices remaining manageable.

Ghana also held at 14% as June inflation rose to 5.3% from 3.7%. Utility tariffs, Middle East escalation and crude were upside risks relative to its 6%–10% medium-term target band. Sri Lanka kept its overnight rate at 8.75% following a 100-basis-point May increase, despite inflation exceeding the 5% target for a third month. Turkey was expected to hold the one-week repo rate at 37% for a fourth meeting while continuing to fund through the 40% overnight rate, awaiting clearer July inflation and energy developments.

Local and external access also differed. Zambia's kwacha bonds had returned 36% in dollar terms this year, against 1.35% for a broad EM local-debt index, supported by copper income and expectations of policy continuity. Yields ranged from 14.25% at the short end to 17.5% further out; the election result was expected to influence the next auction. Tanzania was testing appetite through a London roadshow for its first hard-currency issue since 2013, within plans for about $1.7 billion of foreign borrowing.

Argentina's better sovereign sentiment had not repaired household credit. Bank delinquencies reached a two-decade high after rapid loan growth at very high rates, prompting more selective lending and delaying hopes of a borrowing-led recovery. EMB's 0.30% fall to 95.09 thus encompassed strong Gulf issuance, favorable Thai supply and much tighter conditions elsewhere, even without a new dollar surge.

## Oil and gold rise without a broad volatility shock

Brent gained 4.79% to $95.37 and WTI 3.34% to $87.75. The size of the move brought energy directly into the day's higher breakevens and shorter Treasury yields. Exporters with buffers and importers facing subsidy and current-account costs would experience that pressure differently.

Equities were mixed. The S&P 500 fell 0.14% and the Nasdaq 100 0.54%, but semiconductors gained 0.44%; VIX declined 2.40% to 16.64. Chip buying lifted the broader market from session lows while investors awaited clearer evidence of returns on heavy AI expenditure. The semiconductor index still stood 13.47% below a month earlier, so a positive close did not resolve the financing and valuation debate.

The dollar index eased 0.06% to 101.122, although it remained 0.62% higher over the week. Higher real yields and oil were enough to weigh on EM bonds without another daily currency shock. Gold gained 1.50% to $4,132.10 despite the real-yield increase, as geopolitical hedging outweighed that usual headwind. Energy and policy concerns were therefore visible without a corresponding surge in equity volatility or a wholesale loss of financing confidence.

## Data and new issues will test the limits of the repricing

New-home sales on July 24, advance durable-goods orders on July 27 and advance economic indicators on July 28 lead into the July 28–29 FOMC. The releases will help determine whether demand remains firm enough for the energy shock to prompt a stronger policy response, or whether high borrowing costs are already delivering sufficient restraint.

Galaxy Digital's expected July 23 pricing is a direct test of US high-yield capacity after the Nordic setbacks. Size, yield and secondary performance will show whether the CoreWeave lease and proposed amortization are enough to support the planned $3.5 billion issue near 9%. A completed transaction would establish workable terms for this structure, not unlimited capacity for the sector's financing pipeline.

The SARB decision on July 23 and BOJ meeting on July 31 will show how imported energy is affecting different policy frameworks. South Africa's choice turns partly on second-round effects and expectations; Japan's on underlying inflation, currency pass-through and the pace of normalization. Their guidance will matter for local front ends and currencies, while Japan's long-bond absorption remains relevant to the supply of savings available for foreign duration.
